t.1.12.1: When spring had come round again, a full year was complete; and having saluted Vasiṣṭha and duly honored him in return, according to custom,
t.1.12.3: Let it be arranged so that no obstacle arises in any part of the sacrifice. You are my affectionate friend, and you are my supreme teacher.
t.1.12.2: For the sake of offspring, he spoke courteous words to that best of the twice-born: "O brahmin, O bull among sages, let a sacrifice be performed for me as it has been prescribed."
t.1.12.5: "I shall do all this that has been proposed by you." Then he spoke to the aged brahmins who were well established in the rites of sacrifice.
t.1.12.4: "The burden of the sacrifice that has been undertaken must be borne by you." And that best of the twice-born said to the king, "So be it."
t.1.12.6: And also those well versed in the science of building, aged and supremely righteous, along with overseers of works, artisans, carpenters and diggers as well.
t.1.12.7: Astrologers and craftsmen, and likewise actors and dancers, as well as men who are pure, versed in the śāstras, and deeply learned.
t.1.12.8: "By the king's command, may you, sirs, undertake the work of the sacrifice; let bricks by the many thousands be brought quickly," he said.
t.1.12.9: Let lodgings endowed with many excellent qualities be prepared for the kings, and likewise auspicious dwellings for the brāhmaṇas must be built by the hundreds.
t.1.12.11: Let lodgings be prepared, stocked with abundant food and furnished with every comfort; and likewise for the people of the countryside, let there be many splendid provisions.
t.1.12.10: Well built and furnished with plenty of food, grain and drink, spacious lodgings of the same kind must also be prepared for the people of the city.
t.1.12.12: Food must be given according to proper rule, with due respect and not carelessly, so that people of all varṇas, well honored, receive proper reverence.
t.1.12.13: And no contempt should be shown, not even under the sway of desire or anger, toward the men who are diligently engaged in the sacrificial rites, nor likewise toward the craftsmen.
t.1.12.14: They too must be honored with special care, each in due order, so that everything is well arranged and nothing at all is neglected.
t.1.12.15: "So may you, sirs, act accordingly, with hearts tender with affection." Then all of them, coming together, spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.12.16: "We shall do just as you have said; nothing will be left undone." Then Vasiṣṭha summoned Sumantra and spoke these words.
t.1.12.17: Invite the kings who are on the earth and who are righteous, and Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras too, by the thousands.
t.1.12.18: Bring here, with due honour, the men in all the lands, and the valiant Janaka, lord of Mithilā, whose prowess is true.
t.1.12.19: Bring that illustrious one, accomplished in all the śāstras and likewise accomplished in the Vedas, yourself, with all due honour; knowing him to be a former relation, I therefore tell you this beforehand.
t.1.12.20: Likewise, you yourself must bring the lord of Kāśī, who is affectionate, ever pleasant of speech, of virtuous conduct and like a god.
t.1.12.21: Likewise, bring here the king of the Kekayas, aged and supremely righteous, the father-in-law of this lion among kings, together with his son.
t.1.12.22: Bring here, duly honored, the illustrious Romapāda, the greatly fortunate lord of the Aṅgas, that glorious friend of the lion among kings.
t.1.12.24: And whatever other kings there are upon the face of the earth who are friendly to us, bring them here as swiftly as possible, together with their followers and their kinsmen.
t.1.12.23: Bring here the eastern rulers, the Sindhusauvīras and the kings of Saurāṣṭra, and all the lords of men of the south as well.
t.1.12.25: Having heard those words of Vasiṣṭha, Sumantra then swiftly appointed worthy men there for the task of bringing the kings.
t.1.12.26: At the sage's command, the righteous Sumantra himself set out in haste to bring the kings together.
t.1.12.27: And all those overseers of the work reported to the wise Vasiṣṭha everything that had been prepared for the sacrifice.
t.1.12.28: Then the best of the twice-born, pleased, spoke again to all of them: "Nothing should be given to anyone with contempt, or even carelessly, as if in play. What is done with contempt would destroy the giver; of this there is no doubt."
t.1.12.29: Then, after some days and nights, the kings arrived, bringing many jewels for King Daśaratha.
t.1.12.30: Then Vasiṣṭha, greatly pleased, spoke these words to the king: "O tiger among men, the kings have arrived at your command."
t.1.12.31: All the best of kings have been duly honored by me as befits each, and, O King, the sacrificial preparations have been made by men fully attentive to their work.
t.1.12.32: Let Your Majesty go forth to sacrifice at the sacrificial ground close at hand, which is furnished on every side with all desired things that have been brought there.
t.1.12.33: Then, at the word of both Vasiṣṭha and Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, the lord of the earth set out on an auspicious day under an auspicious lunar asterism.
t.1.12.34: Then all the foremost of the twice-born, led by Vasiṣṭha, placing Ṛṣyaśṛṅga at their head, began the work of the sacrifice at that time.
